radiology_report:
Radiology Division | Erasmus MC University Medical Center | 08 Jan 2025
Exam: Multiparametric MRI Prostate

Clinical context: Re-evaluation of prior prostate cancer diagnosis. Current PSA 6.5 ng/mL. Previous PI-RADS 4 lesion identified.

FINDINGS:
The gland measures 59.14 mL in volume. T2-weighted sequences highlight a focal hypointense abnormality within the left mid peripheral zone, spanning roughly 11 mm along its longest axis. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows pronounced restriction with correspondingly low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences demonstrate early, focal enhancement compared to adjacent parenchyma. There is no evidence of extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion. Pelvic lymph nodes remain unremarkable in size. The bladder and distal urethra appear normal.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the left mid peripheral zone.
Prostate volume 59.14 mL, PSA density 0.11 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.7465537.

previous_notes.author: Dr. K. Bakker (GP)
previous_notes.text: During a consultation on 13 Sep 2024, Dr. K. Bakker documented a PSA escalation from 4.5 ng/mL recorded in May 2024 to 5.1 ng/mL at that visit. In light of the patient's history of a prior positive biopsy alongside this upward trajectory, a follow-up PSA was requested; the subsequent result of 6.5 ng/mL triggered this urology referral for clinical assessment.
